chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Abdullah ibn Talha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption in the land is that they be killed,' the Verse. This is the exile of the combatant; it is other than this exile. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The ruler rules upon him according to what he has done, and he is exiled and carried in the sea, then thrown by it. If the exile is from one city to another, as if his expulsion is from one city to another, it is equivalent to the killing, and the crucifixion, and the cutting, but the Penalty (Hadd) is that which corresponds to the cutting and the crucifixion.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific meaning of 'exile' in the verse of Qital according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential application of Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:33, distinguishing the specific mode of 'exile' (nafy) as transporting the offender to sea and casting them in, rather than mere land-based banishment. It establishes that this penalty is discretionary, calibrated by the ruler (al-hakim) to match the severity of the crime, serving as an equivalent alternative to execution, crucifixion, or amputation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Hafs, from Abdullah asws Bin Talha, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws

regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:33] But rather, the Recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Rasool and strive to make mischief in the land is only this, that they should be killed – the Verse. This is an exiling of the combatant, it is other than the (general) exiling’. Heasws said: ‘The ruler would issue a ruling upon him in accordance with what he had done, and he would be exiled, and he would be carried in the sea, then thrown by it, if it was the exiling from a city to another city, as if his exit happens to be from a city to another city, being justice, of the killing, and the crucifixion, and the cutting, but the Penalty (Hadd) happens to be in accordance with the cutting and the crucifixion’.
